note: Thursday 5 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run. The dominant story is the Nov 3 US midterm election result -- a Democratic sweep of House and Senate confirmed overnight -- which drove Wednesday's huge risk-on/vol-crush session (VIX -20.3%, Dow +3.03%) and the gold/silver/miners surge that is the single best session for the levered-silver leg of this book in months. 5 of 14 items are from the last 24 hours (Nov 5) and 9 more from Nov 4.

items.headline: Democrats sweep House and Senate in US midterms, ending divided-government uncertainty
items.summary: AP called the Senate for Democrats and then called the House as well on election night Nov 3 into Nov 4, flipping both chambers for only the fifth time since WWII in a midterm. House Speaker Mike Johnson announced he will not seek re-election as GOP leader; Sherrod Brown, Jon Ossoff and other Democrats won key Senate races.
items.actionable: Removal of election-outcome uncertainty was the single biggest catalyst behind Wednesday's broad risk-on move, including the gold/silver/miners leg of this portfolio, and sets up a gridlock narrative that markets are reading as policy-predictable rather than destabilizing.

items.headline: VIX crashes 20% as Wall Street posts biggest post-midterm rally in 44 years
items.summary: The VIX plunged 20.26% to 16.61 as election uncertainty cleared; the Dow jumped 1,569.40 points (+3.03%) to 53,356.12, the S&P 500 gained 1.58% and the Nasdaq rose 1.44%. Gainers outnumbered decliners roughly 3-to-1, with the rally broadening beyond tech as oil's steep slide added momentum.
items.actionable: The volatility collapse confirms the midterm result is being priced as a de-risking event, not a new source of policy shock, which argues for holding through Fed/BOE/NFP catalysts this week rather than hedging into them.

items.headline: Gold vaults back above $4,000 and silver jumps to $52.49 as dollar and yields drop post-election
items.summary: Spot gold rose 2.95% to $4,053.68/oz and silver gained 4.58% to $52.49/oz as the dollar weakened and Treasury yields fell following the Democratic sweep. Gold ETFs absorbed 211 tonnes on the day, lifting global holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes.
items.actionable: This is the direct driver of the GDX/SILJ/HL/NEM leg of the portfolio's best day in months; record ETF inflows suggest the move has institutional participation rather than being purely a short-covering spike, supporting continued long exposure.

items.headline: Oil extends slide below $100 Brent as Iran reopens door to Hormuz deal and Trump plays down new strikes
items.summary: Brent crude fell below $100/bbl and WTI slipped near $95.20 after Trump told the Financial Times the US has no immediate plans for further strikes on Iran and Tehran signaled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Traders are now watching for a signed US-Iran agreement on shipping security through the Strait.
items.actionable: No direct oil holdings in the portfolio, but a de-escalating Hormuz risk premium removes a tail-risk input into the macro backdrop and supports the broader risk-on tone benefiting equities/miners; watch for any reversal if Hormuz talks stall again before the Nov 10 rare-earth truce deadline.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export truce, due to expire Nov 10, reportedly extended to Jan 10 2027 after Trump-Xi summit -- but Beijing hasn't published matching legal text
items.summary: China's October 2025 suspension of its harshest rare-earth export add-on controls was set to lapse Nov 10, 2026; a MOFCOM official said after the Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit that the arrangement is extended to Jan 10, 2027, though no formal notice has been issued. Separately, the April 2025 licensing regime covering seven medium/heavy rare earths was never suspended and remains in force.
items.actionable: If the extension holds, it reduces near-term supply-shock risk for SMIC/Xiaomi and global tech, which is incrementally bearish for the US/allied rare-earth buildout thesis (MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels/USA Rare Earth) that trades on China-decoupling urgency -- watch Nov 10 closely for whether Beijing actually codifies the extension or lets it lapse.

items.headline: SMIC surges 8.96% and Hang Seng climbs 1.67% to 23,919.50 as HK tech and gold/AI-supply-chain names lead
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index closed up 393.53 points (+1.67%) at 23,919.50 on Nov 4, led in the afternoon by technology and healthcare shares after an early dip, tracking a mainland rally and reduced global election uncertainty. SMIC (0981.HK) specifically jumped 8.96% on the day.
items.actionable: SMIC's outsized gain within a broad HK tech rally confirms it is trading as a geopolitics/risk-sentiment proxy as much as a fundamentals story -- the midterm clarity and softer US-China tension narrative are the near-term tailwind to monitor for follow-through.

items.headline: Oracle cancels $7 billion AI chip leasing deal with Tencent amid US regulatory pressure
items.summary: Oracle scrapped a $7 billion agreement to lease advanced AI chips to Tencent after US officials raised concerns about China's access to American semiconductor technology. Tencent is separately pursuing AI partnerships in Saudi Arabia and cross-border payment tie-ups with Mastercard and UnionPay.
items.actionable: This is a concrete setback to Tencent's AI compute roadmap and a reminder that US chip-export enforcement, not just tariffs, remains a live overhang on the China/HK tech sleeve even amid the broader risk-on mood; Tencent reports earnings Nov 18, which will show how it is routing around the lost capacity.

items.headline: Singapore bank earnings season: DBS and UOB Q3 both soften; OCBC reports Thursday Nov 6 after Citi 'sell' downgrade
items.summary: DBS reported Q3 net profit down 2% y/y to S$2.95B (beating consensus) with a 75-cent total dividend; UOB posted S$1.25B net profit, down 15% q/q and missing consensus, with record fee income but CET1 easing to 14.6%. OCBC, which Citi downgraded to 'sell' on Oct 6 citing margin pressure, reports its own Q3 results Thu Nov 6.
items.actionable: Bank earnings are coming in softer than headline numbers suggest (UOB miss, margin compression flagged by Citi for OCBC), which matters given the large STI weighting of these three names in the SGX sleeve; OCBC's Nov 6 print is the next read-through for whether the NIM-compression thesis is sector-wide.

items.headline: Energy Fuels reports Q3 2026 results, approves construction of commercial-scale heavy rare earth oxide circuits at White Mesa Mill
items.summary: Energy Fuels announced Q3 2026 results and board approval to begin construction of commercial-scale heavy rare earth oxide separation circuits at its White Mesa Mill. The move follows its ASM acquisition adding rare-earth metal/alloy production and sits alongside a pending VAC acquisition, as the company builds an integrated Western mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain.
items.actionable: Concrete capacity-expansion news (not just policy talk) for a core rare-earths watchlist name, directly relevant to the thesis that Western heavy-rare-earth separation capacity is the scarce bottleneck China's export truce is designed to exploit.

items.headline: MP Materials reports Q3 2026 earnings after market close today, with analysts expecting a small loss
items.summary: MP Materials is scheduled to post Q3 2026 results after the close on Thursday Nov 5, with consensus looking for a loss of 1 cent per share on revenue of about $118.86 million. The print comes as MP continues to ramp its DoD-backed magnet facility amid the broader rare-earth capacity buildout.
items.actionable: This is the next binary catalyst for the rare-earths watchlist -- guidance on magnet-facility ramp and any commentary on the Nov 10 China truce deadline will matter more than the headline EPS miss/beat for MP and by extension sentiment toward LYC.AX/UUUU/USAR.

items.headline: JL Mag Rare-Earth (6680.HK) repurchases 800,000 H-shares, citing undervaluation
items.summary: JL MAG Rare-Earth bought back 800,000 H shares on Nov 4 for roughly HK$11.69 million at an average price of HK$14.6155 per share. The company said the buyback reflects its view that shares are undervalued and it intends to cancel the repurchased shares, reducing registered capital.
items.actionable: A small but fresh signal of management confidence from the one rare-earth-magnet pure play on the watchlist with direct HK-listed exposure, worth tracking alongside the Nov 10 China truce deadline for read-through to magnet-maker economics.

items.headline: Fed speakers Hammack, Barkin, Williams, Musalem and Bowman on the wire this week after a run of hawkish 'rates need to be higher' comments
items.summary: Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack speaks Thursday Nov 5, followed by Richmond Fed's Barkin; New York Fed's Williams speaks Friday Nov 6, with Musalem and Bowman also on the calendar Friday. This follows recent comments from several Fed officials that rates may need to stay higher for longer given sticky inflation.
items.actionable: Any hawkish tilt from these speakers could cap the dollar-weakness tailwind that drove Wednesday's gold/silver surge, so this is the key macro input to watch before the Nov 6 payrolls print.

items.headline: Bank of England decision due today, markets pricing ~96% odds of a hike to 4.00%
items.summary: The BOE's rate announcement is due at 12:00 UK time Thursday Nov 5, alongside its Monetary Policy Report. A Reuters poll had 54 of 63 economists forecasting a 25bp hike to 4.00%, and OIS pricing as of Nov 4 implied roughly a 96% probability of that outcome.
items.actionable: A widely-expected BOE hike is unlikely to move this portfolio directly, but a surprise hold or dovish guidance would add to the global rate-cut/weak-dollar narrative that has been supportive of gold and silver this week -- worth a quick check given timing lands between today's Fed speakers and tomorrow's NFP.

items.headline: US October nonfarm payrolls due Friday, consensus around 65K after September's steep 29K miss
items.summary: The BLS October jobs report is scheduled for release Friday Nov 6, with consensus estimates clustered around 60-65K (Barclays specifically estimates 50K), following a weak September print of just 29K versus a 90K forecast. The report will be closely watched as a labor-market health check after a run of soft prints.
items.actionable: A weak print (in line with or below September's miss) would reinforce the dovish-Fed, weak-dollar backdrop that has been bullish for gold/silver/miners this week, while a strong beat could trigger a reversal in the dollar and pressure the precious-metals rally -- the single most important scheduled data point for this portfolio over the next 24 hours.
